summaries.label: First Reading
summaries.text: Paul says those who live by faith are children of Abraham, and that God’s promise to bless all nations in Abraham is fulfilled in Christ, who took on himself the curse of the law so that we might receive the promised Spirit through faith.

summaries.label: Psalm
summaries.text: The psalmist praises the Lord’s great works and his compassion. God gives food to those who fear him, remembers his covenant for ever, and gives his people the inheritance of the nations.

summaries.label: Gospel
summaries.text: Some say Jesus casts out demons by Beelzebub. He answers that a divided kingdom falls, that he acts by the finger of God, and that a stronger one has overcome the strong man. A swept house left empty is soon reoccupied by worse spirits.

unity: The promise to Abraham and the finger of God at Sinai both lead to the Spirit given through Christ, who drives out evil. Casting out a fault is not enough: fill the space with prayer and one concrete act of service today.
lead_in: Luke’s “finger of God” recalls the tablets of Sinai, and the Spirit promised in Galatians is that same finger writing on human hearts.

excerpt.text: The finger. “It is by the finger of God that [Jesus] cast out demons.” If God’s law was written on tablets of stone “by the finger of God,” then the “letter from Christ” entrusted to the care of the apostles, is written “with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone, but on tablets of human hearts.” The hymn Veni Creator Spiritus invokes the Holy Spirit as the “finger of the Father’s right hand.”
